claims.text: The initial as-cast alloy has a metastable microstructure.
The initial microstructure contains supersaturated solid solutions.
The initial microstructure contains dispersed intermetallic compounds.
The alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
Thermal aging promotes solute partitioning in non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Thermally activated diffusion partitions Mg and other elements from the metastable matrix.
Solute partitioning increases the bulk volume fraction of equilibrium intermetallic compounds.
Aging under oxidizing conditions forms a continuous Mg/Al-rich surface oxide scale.
The Mg/Al-rich oxide scale is dense and protective.
The Mg/Al-rich surface oxide improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Improved oxidation resistance will be expressed as lower oxidation mass gain relative to the as-cast state.
Bulk phase evolution changes local electrochemical behavior.
Changes in local electrochemical behavior alter corrosion performance in aggressive chloride environments.
Thermally aged alloys may exhibit lower corrosion current density or modified pitting behavior relative to the as-cast state.
The initial as-cast alloy lacks a continuous protective surface oxide.
The proposed mechanism applies to Mg-containing high-entropy alloys below 6 g/cm3, including MgAlCuZnGd-type systems.
Constituent-property differences and oxidation kinetics are key drivers of phase evolution in the bounded alloy class.
Interior intermetallic compounds may produce detrimental cathodic effects that influence corrosion performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted corrosion outcome is framed mainly as an unspecified alteration, including modified pitting behavior, whereas the falsification rule requires corrosion performance to improve. A changed but non-improved corrosion response could therefore satisfy the stated prediction while also being classified as falsifying.
